item.title: Managing Clinical Depression Symptoms
item.description:
Clinical depression affects more than 21 million people in the United States annually. The mental condition is also referred to as Major Depressive Disorder. When an individual experiences the symptoms of clinical depression consistently for more than two weeks, a mental health professional may diagnose them with the mental disorder.

Common Clinical Depression Symptoms

Clinical depression symptoms interfere with daily activities, including pleasurable hobbies, as well as relationships and goals. Depression can feel like a dark cloud following you around. You might find it difficult to resume daily responsibilities. Autopilot becomes your way to get through the day, and for many, getting out of bed feels like too much effort.

The following are some clinical depression symptoms you may experience:

Persistent sadness – Sadness that hangs on for two weeks or more and interferes with daily activities. You may not be able to identify why you feel sad or empty. You may feel numbness to things around you.

Fatigue – A bone-weary tiredness that leaves you with little energy to do anything. You might sit on the couch or lie in bed. The fatigue makes it so you only do the things you absolutely have no choice but to do.

Sleep problems – Trouble falling or staying asleep or sleeping too much can leave you groggy in the morning. The brain needs time to recover and repair during the night, and sleep deprivation can lead to higher levels of the stress hormone, cortisol.

Loss of interest – Losing the joy and pleasure you once had for favorite activities. This can include hobbies, activities, events, movies, music, work, or school. You may find it draining to socialize even with the people you love most in the world.

Changes in appetite – Depression not only affects stress hormones, but it also alters the hormones responsible for hunger and metabolism. Ghrelin and leptin signal when you are hungry and need to eat, and when you are full or satisfied and need to stop. You may find that you are not hungry much at all or that you overeat as a coping mechanism.

Rapid weight gain or loss – Due to changes in appetite and hormones, you may see a rapid weight gain or loss. If you overeat and suffer from fatigue, the scale may go up, and your clothes might fit tighter. However, if you barely eat and suffer from sleep deprivation, relying on caffeine to keep you going, you may lose a considerable amount of weight.

Trouble concentrating – Trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks due to depression is common. With the lack of motivation and the increased fatigue, it can be hard to recall important details or complete work projects. You may leave projects half done or frequently lose items.

Mood swings – Irritability, anger, and mood swings can also develop with depression. You feel as if you shouldn’t be bothered by others, and little things may make you angry. You might snap at your family or coworkers more often or have an outburst of anger and cry when you least expect it.

Feeling guilty, ashamed, or worthless – The empty feeling from depression can also leave you with feelings of guilt, shame, regret, and worthlessness. You might feel that no matter what you do, nothing gets better. Depression robs you of joy, but the mental condition is not permanent, and it is treatable. You are more than these emotions.

Headaches and unexplained body aches – Headaches and body aches can worsen depression symptoms, but depression alters brain chemistry and pain perception. You may experience more frequent, unexplained aches and pains. This can make you feel worse. Consult with your counselor and physician about pain management combined with therapy.

Suicidal ideations – Negative thoughts, intense emotions, and impulses can lead you to self-harm or suicidal ideations. Talk therapy and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy could help alleviate depression symptoms and help you challenge negative thoughts.

If you are having suicidal thoughts or thoughts of harming others, seek help immediately.

How to Manage Symptoms

The symptoms of depression can affect physical and emotional health. Learning to make small changes and instill new, healthier habits can help relieve symptoms when combined with therapy. In some cases, your physician may recommend medication. Your mental health care plan should be well-rounded.

The following is a list of things you can do to manage symptoms.

Seeking Professional Help

A professional mental health provider can diagnose clinical depression and create a plan to manage and overcome the symptoms. Seek professional help if you experience symptoms consistently for more than two weeks or have thoughts of self-harm or suicide.

Getting Better Quality Sleep

Prioritizing sleep by creating a nightly routine and going to bed earlier can help your brain recover and repair. Sleeping seven to nine hours nightly can lower adrenaline and cortisol levels, stress hormones that, when high, can worsen depression and anxiety.

Reducing Stress

You can reduce stress further by slowing down. Whether that is practicing deep breathing or moving into stretching poses, slowing down releases tension. Try a physical relaxation technique known as Progressive Muscle Relaxation to learn how to identify areas of tension in the body. Lie down on a bed or the floor, and starting with the toes, systematically tense body parts for a few seconds and then release. Move through the body, tensing and relaxing. Breathe deeply during each round.

Exercising Daily

Exercise is God’s way of giving us a little mood boost throughout the day. It also improves physical health. The brain releases serotonin, dopamine, and other chemicals that naturally lower stress hormones and leave you feeling happier, more confident, and accomplished. A brisk 30-minute walk in the morning, most days of the week, could help you feel more relaxed and happier. For physical benefits, aim for 150 minutes or more of moderate-intensity movement weekly.

Avoiding Ultra-Processed Foods

Ultra-processed foods, foods and beverages with added chemicals, sugars, and preservatives, can worsen depression symptoms. These types of food alter bacteria in the gut, which is correlated with brain function. Aim for healthier foods, such as lean proteins, healthy fats, fresh fruits and vegetables, and whole grains when possible.

Limiting Alcohol

Alcohol can trigger depression in some people and worsen symptoms. People may overdrink to cope with uncomfortable or painful emotions. Alcohol may make them feel better temporarily by numbing those emotions. However, the individual feels worse after the alcohol wears off and eventually will need to consume more alcohol to get that same feeling.

It is not uncommon for someone struggling with alcoholism and depression to start drinking with a can or two of beer or glasses of wine and find themselves years later drinking a case of beer or a bottle of wine before bed to gain the same effect. If you struggle with alcohol, reach out for help.

Seeking Help for Substance Abuse

Much like alcohol, substances like illegal drugs and prescription drugs can alter brain chemistry and worsen depression and anxiety. Abusing prescription drugs or taking illegal “street” drugs will require professional help to stop and manage withdrawal symptoms in a safe environment, whether that is at home with supervision or under a doctor’s care in a facility.

As with alcohol, the brain builds a tolerance to drugs, and it takes more to receive the same effect. Giving the body time to detox and receive nourishment in the form of healthy foods and physical activity can alleviate the severity of some depression symptoms.

Help for Clinical Depression Symptoms

Don’t struggle with clinical depression symptoms another day. Reach out to our center to schedule a session with a Christian counselor. Depression is a common but challenging mental health disorder that requires therapy and lifestyle changes.

We offer help by connecting you to a counselor for an assessment. Afterward, you and your counselor create a customized care plan to manage clinical depression symptoms so you can move forward. Give us a call today.

item.title: Preventing Infidelity Through a Faith-Based Lifestyle
item.description:
Marriage and its faithful foundation are deeper than promises spoken at an altar on a wedding day. Temptation exists because we live in a world that revolves around attention. Creating a solid framework for a successful marriage requires intentional choices to foster a lifestyle of fidelity.

Using biblical truth, a couple can cultivate a lifestyle that will strengthen their marriage. Preventing infidelity requires more from each spouse than hope alone. They must actively work together on their relationship, using positive reinforcement and emotional connection.

Couples cannot assume their commitment ceremony was enough of a foundation for a solid marriage. This thought process can create a vulnerable space where the pressures of life can erode what should be their strongest connection. The best marriage advice states that prevention requires ongoing actions and effort, not just promises in the beginning.

Preventing infidelity through faith-based approaches acknowledges human weakness and divine strength. These approaches create a practical framework that addresses the hard issues rather than managing temptation. Christian counseling emphasizes that lifelong fidelity comes from the transformed hearts and renewed minds of the spouses. This happens when couples build a relationship on biblical principles that create a habit of good choices.

But because of the temptation to sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife and each woman her own husband. – 1 Corinthians 7:2, ESV

Building Spiritual Intimacy Before Physical Intimacy

The greatest connections occur when spouses prioritize their spiritual bonds. This doesn’t mean the physical attraction or romance isn’t important. Rather, that spiritual intimacy will affect the foundation that makes physical intimacy meaningful and long-lasting. By praying, studying scripture, and pursuing God together, the couple will create a unique connection that the world cannot replicate.

Quite often, affairs do not begin with physical attraction. They start with an emotional connection that fills the gap in the primary relationship. By building spiritual intimacy, the couple can directly address this vulnerability. Spouses who share their deepest beliefs, fears, and hopes based on faith create emotional intimacy that becomes a protective barrier. This level of connection reflects the shallowness of outside relationships.

Building spiritual intimacy requires intentional effort. Faith-based marriage advice suggests that prayer and scripture reading together be intentional. Discussions of faith must apply to daily decisions and future dreams. Christian counselors consistently see that couples who maintain these disciplines have lower infidelity risks. A crucial factor is that a spiritual connection fosters emotional security, making temptation less appealing.

A faith-based approach will also address the deeper issue of identity and purpose. Spouses who understand their worth and calling through their personal relationship with God are less likely to seek validation outside of a marriage. Spiritual growth often fills the emptiness that drives infidelity. Spiritual connection can create a positive cycle, allowing spiritual intimacy to strengthen the marriage, which deepens spiritual intimacy.

Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it. – Proverbs 4:23, ESV

Establishing Clear Communication and Boundaries

Open communication about boundaries is about creating safety and not suspicion. Often, behaviors that threaten relationships aren’t discussed until the problem arises. This type of reactive approach will lead the marriage to a defensive position when the spouses should be proactive. Effective marriage advice often includes having honest conversations about interactions with others before those interactions become problematic.

When a couple establishes clear boundaries early in the marriage, there will be less conflict around fidelity issues. These awkward conversations will create shared understanding in terms of expectations and limits. The goal is not to control one another; it is to protect through a mutual agreement. When each spouse understands what behavior crosses the line, they will make better choices in the challenging situation.

Boundary setting can cover various areas of interaction with others. The most common areas are social media connections, workplace relationships, and friendships that stem from former romantic relationships.

Another important aspect is the emotional boundaries set regarding intimate details of the marriage. This means spouses should not seek emotional support outside the relationship. Christian counseling recognizes that these boundaries offer protection from compromising situations for either spouse.

One major aspect of relationships is communication. This area requires ongoing dialogue instead of one-time conversations. Boundaries may need adjustment through discussion because of changing circumstances.

Regular communication from each spouse regarding how they feel about various relationships and situations will prevent major problems. This is called proactive communication. It builds trust for both spouses because they know they can address concerns openly without judgment.

Therefore, having put away falsehood, let each one of you speak the truth with his neighbor, for we are members one of another. – Ephesians 4:25, ESV

Creating Accountability in the Faith Community

Infidelity happens more easily when there’s isolation. Affairs happen in secret and thrive on deception. These hidden connections create isolation. Couples actively engaged in faith communities create natural accountability systems that will discourage secret behavior. This is not about having a watchful eye, but about maintaining relationships that will reinforce the marriage commitment.

Strong communities and faith foundations provide multiple layers of support for marriages. Marriage advice from experienced couples can model faithful relationships to those who are just starting their marriage journey.

Social connections that include both spouses reduce opportunities for one-on-one relationships that may be inappropriate. These communities can also provide spiritual guidance through pastors and Christian counselors who understand that each marriage may face unique challenges.

Accountability works through visibility and relationships. By regularly attending church, participating in small groups, and maintaining friendships with other committed couples, a marriage can be reinforced. A strong social support system will have an impact on relationship satisfaction and the rate of infidelity. Communities of faith that promote marriage and family values provide this support naturally.

Many couples can benefit from specific relationships with mentoring couples or same gender friends who can provide guidance and support. These relationships offer safe spaces for discussing temptations, challenges, and concerns. The key is to choose the accountability partner who shares the same values and provides encouragement and honest feedback.

And though a man might prevail against one who is alone, two will withstand him – a threefold cord is not quickly broken. – Ecclesiastes 4:12, ESV

Strengthening Marriage Through Shared Faith Practices

For there to be unity in marriage, there needs to be intentional cultivation of shared experiences that reinforce the bond. Practice is based on faith and provides structured opportunities for spouses to grow together instead of drifting apart. Worshipping together, serving together, and pursuing spiritual growth together create shared memories and purposes that will strengthen the bond between spouses.

These regularly shared faith practices address one of the primary vulnerabilities that lead to infidelity: growing apart over time. When a couple maintains shared activities and goals, they will experience deeper satisfaction in their marriage.

Faith-based activities create a natural structure for this connection. As they attend weekly worship services and share daily devotions, the spiritual discussions create consistent touchpoints that will help encourage emotional intimacy.

One area that strengthens marriages unexpectedly is serving together. As they work toward a common goal beyond their immediate needs, they experience the satisfaction of accomplishment. Volunteering together to support others in their community creates a partnership and reinforces their sense of being a team. Christian counseling often promotes service activities as a way to build relationships.

When couples pray together, there is a unique intimacy that goes beyond emotional or even physical connection. Couples will develop spiritual intimacy when they pray for their loved ones and community together. This reduces the appeal of external relationships. It will also create an opportunity for discussion of concerns through the lens of faith. This will create a stronger commitment that will naturally resist the outside threats.

Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh. – Genesis 2:24, ESV

Developing a Stronger Relationship with Support

Preventing infidelity in a marriage requires both spouses to be intentional in building a partnership that will withstand outside influences. Faith-based lifestyles are known to experience a stronger bond between spouses. This bond will create an environment where fidelity flows naturally.

For more information regarding a faith-based program for preventing infidelity, contact your local Christian counselor services today.

item.title: How to Forgive Yourself for Betraying Your Partner
item.description:
A relationship is forever changed the moment a person cheats on their partner. One choice, often fueled by deep issues that went unseen, causes trauma, heartache, and often the dissolution of a relationship or marriage. As the guilty party, you can more easily navigate this chapter if you remain humble, honest, and willing to face the consequences of your choices.

Though you have caused much grief and pain, and even if things will never be the same again, you are not beyond redemption. A part of anyone’s journey to becoming a better person involves learning how to forgive yourself for some of your worst mistakes.

Why did you do it?

There are a million reasons why people cheat, and none of them are a justification for doing it. However, when you are forced to think honestly about why you crossed a boundary in a relationship or marriage, it is the beginning of understanding yourself and your beliefs.

You might have felt entitled to do it, you might have been impulsive about it, or you might have been calculating in your actions. Before you can learn how to forgive yourself, you need to know what you are forgiving yourself for.

Infidelity is not always sexual in nature. Even when it seems entirely about physical attraction and sex, there is often something deeper that is ultimately motivating you to cheat. Betrayal doesn’t happen by accident, even when it escalates from an impulsive choice. You had forethought, intention, and, deeper than that, a belief about the relationship you’re in and the partner you’re with.

For example, you might believe that a bit of flirtation is fun and harmless. Maybe you’ve seen your partner flirt with others. You might think that the relationship has become stale to the point that a secret tryst wouldn’t affect your partner. You might believe that you have become so unattractive in your older age that anyone who looks at you with desire is hard to resist.

Beliefs like these are like the rudders on a ship. They are small and unseen, but they determine the direction of the ship. If you were to ask yourself why you cheated, what answer would you give? When you have answered honestly, consider how your answer reflects your beliefs about the relationship, your partner, or yourself.

Hard Truths About Forgiveness

It may take months and even years to discover what motivated you to betray your partner. Despite this, your partner will often demand it of you as they try to understand your choices. You owe them an explanation, even when you haven’t understood your own actions. In moments alone, try as much as you can to reflect on yourself, your choices, and your underlying beliefs. That will help you communicate with your partner, though they might not understand or accept what you tell them.

Here are some hard truths about forgiveness:

Your partner is not obligated to forgive you

They are their own person, with their own issues, making their own choices. It’s true that if they don’t forgive you, it will likely affect them negatively for the rest of their lives and affect their future relationships. But they are not obligated to forgive, and likely will not soon forget. Betrayal is a form of trauma, and even the simplest trauma takes between three and five years to move on from.

Forgiveness is complex and might not repair the relationship

Forgiveness is a complicated, messy journey that goes back and forth through tangled emotions and sometimes makes things more complicated. Like with physical injuries, betrayal trauma leaves a scar long after the wound has healed. It serves as a reminder for the person not to trust so easily again, or to be less generous with their heart.

Forgiving and forgetting hardly ever go hand in hand. You might have changed their life forever, not for the better.

You cannot move on until you’ve found forgiveness, and that means you have to learn how to forgive yourself

They might not find it easy to forgive, but you must learn how to forgive yourself. Self-forgiveness does not come easily. All too often, people are crippled by the shame and guilt of what they did. Other times, people protect themselves by being proud of their choices, believing they don’t require forgiveness.

You need to come to the point where you can acknowledge where you went wrong and recognize that you are better than your worst choices.

How to Forgive Yourself

You might have wrecked everything and changed people’s lives forever. You are still worthy of forgiveness. You can still move forward, making better choices, even when you can’t make up for the mistakes you made in the past. People often think that forgiveness is the same as wiping the slate clean and starting over again. It can be that, but never in the case of infidelity and cheating.

You haven’t made a mess on the counter that can be cleaned up and forgotten. You have taken an ax to a tree and hacked away, even if the cheating was a singular event. You have not only changed the relationship forever, but you have changed the way your loved one sees you, and the way you see yourself. It will take years for that tree of trust to grow back, if it ever does.

Here are some steps you can take to walk toward healing and learn how to forgive yourself:

Be honest

The first step to coming clean is honesty. In this instance, honesty begins with confessing what you did, and continues with reflecting on what motivated you, and what you want. It might feel shameful to admit to failures and weaknesses in your character, but it’s more shameful still to pretend, lie, and gaslight. Learning how to forgive yourself begins with being brutally honest about your choices and your character.

Accept blame

It’s tempting to point your fingers at your partner and your relationship, but you will never learn how to forgive yourself if you blame everyone else for what happened. If you are both willing to work on the relationship, you will both have to take responsibility for rebuilding it. That cannot happen until you have taken ownership of your failures, regardless of your partners’ mistakes, faults, and flaws.

Continue working on yourself

You have a future, even if your relationship does not. Your choices might have destroyed the chances of a future with your loved one, but there is still a future for both of you, even if it is apart. Regardless of how it feels, you do not have to forever live in the shame and guilt of what you did. You still have an opportunity to go forward armed with a deeper knowledge of where you are broken, and most importantly, what you want in the future.

There is hope

You might have made the biggest mistake of your life, and it might affect you for years to come, but you are not beyond hope. There might be a long way to go as you try to make things right, and ultimately, it might not work out. What matters is that you are willing to be honest, to accept the blame for what you did, and to work on yourself in the future.

You can still learn how to forgive yourself and move on as a changed person. You might be a little scarred and heartbroken, but your greatest mistake can teach you how to be humble, honest, and willing to do what it takes to make things right.

It’s not always easy to talk about your failures, even with friends. When you meet with a counselor, you are meeting in a confidential space with someone who will listen and reflect, but never judge. That doesn’t mean the sessions will always be easy, because working on yourself never is. However, if you would like to start counseling to move toward healing and hope, please contact us for more information.

item.title: 5 Ways A Vision Board Can Help You Embrace the New Year
item.description:
The new year is a time for people to make New Year’s resolutions or choose a word for the year they live by. People choose the new year to make goals to help them find their character, and they can set goals to improve various aspects of their lives.

Some people who want to avoid making New Year’s resolutions choose one word instead. For example, people may select the word hope and decide to live each day by incorporating that word into their lives. No matter whether a person chooses to use resolutions or one word, people need to look forward to the future.

Another way to do that is to create a vision board. A vision board is a physical representation of the goals people want to set for their lives. People can do this on a poster board, a bulletin board, or any other type of material that will help them be reminded of their goals each day.

To create a vision board, a person will cut out pictures from various magazines or print them from the Internet and post them on the board. They may organize them in areas where they want to improve their lives.

They may also want to write captions on the photos to remind them exactly what the goal is that they want to accomplish. Vision boards are an excellent way for people to embrace the new year. They are fun and a quick and easy way for people to create goals, but they also hold themselves accountable for the goals they’ve made for the year.

5 Ways a Vision Board Can Help You Embrace the New Year

Here are five ways a vision board can help you embrace the new year.

It gives people hope

A vision board gives people excitement and hope about the future. Even people who feel they will never achieve their wildest dreams can have hope that it will happen. Because of the prominent place of the board, it’s a visual, practical representation of a person’s goals. The board gives them accountability because it’s essential to try to fulfill the goals discussed on the board.

A vision board is a cheap and easy way to express their goals, use their imaginations, and start dreaming again. Vision boards are great because they can be efficient and allow people to have small goals that they know they can achieve, but also have their wildest dreams. It helps remind people that life is fun and can be enjoyed once again.

It helps people dream again

Vision boards also help people to dream again. Children often use their imaginations. They create through drawing, painting, and other creative mediums. Creating a vision board allows adults to tap into that creative process again. As adults, we stopped being creative because of daily responsibilities and tasks to be completed. We stopped using our imagination.

However, a vision board helps them be creative again in a limited space. The great thing about a vision board is that anything goes with what is placed on it. For example, if a person wants a Ferrari or other expensive car in their lifetime, that can put it on the board.

If a person wants to own a house, they can also do that. It’s fun to be creative and use their imagination to create what life can be if only we work to achieve it. The vision board awakens people’s dreams and makes them a reality.

It gets people motivated

Vision boards are also good because people can write them down in a journal or on paper. But the month usually gets away from us, and soon, the end of January hits, and we have yet to achieve any of the goals we set out to do.

It is easy at that point to throw the paper away or cross out the resolutions and continue to live as we always have. People who are not good at making goals may love the idea of doing away with goals altogether. However, a vision board that is posted where a person can be reminded of their story helps motivate them to progress in life.

A vision board will help people dream about various aspects of their lives that they want to improve. A person can make health goals through exercise and diet, financial goals through wealth management and acquiring possessions and properties, and even have a vision of marriage where they dream of the ideal marriage. Nothing is impossible with the vision board.

The possibilities are endless. Don’t allow reality and an uncreative mind to stop you from allowing your board to be all it can be.

Eventually, people begin to see their lives take shape. This gives them hope for the future. It is easy to think about the baby steps they can take to achieve those goals. Seeing the daily visual reminder will help motivate them to take small steps toward their goals. Because a vision board is open-ended and there are no timelines set for when the goals need to be completed, a person can take baby steps, and it can be months or years before they achieve that goal.

It rids people of guilt

Unlike a New Year’s resolution, there’s no guilt associated with not achieving a goal on time. Any goals posted on the board can take years, but it’s just a matter of how long and what resources and motivation the person needs to achieve them.

New Year’s resolutions fail because people make lofty goals, but they need practical strategies to implement those goals. For example, a person who wants to achieve good health may make an open-ended goal, like they want to lose weight.

However, they need to have measurable, attainable aspects that are related to that goal. The vision board helps people see how they will achieve that goal. For example, for someone’s marriage, they may want to have children. They may post a picture of a baby on the vision board. But that could take a few months or a few years. The good news is that someone doesn’t feel guilty if the goal is not accomplished in a year.

It uses colors and various art forms

Year’s resolutions are static in that they are simply words on a page. Vision boards, however, use various art forms to achieve the board’s purpose. People can use magazine pictures, drawings, typed words, or quotes they’ve seen online or typed out themselves. The possibilities are endless. A person could take it one step further and decorate the outside of the board or even draw on the board in between the pictures.

No matter how they choose to set up their board, the more creative, the better. Because it is their creation, they would be more likely to achieve the goals they set forth on the board if they put the creative aspect into it. Tapping into creativity gives hope that the new year will increase your expectations regarding how it will take shape.

When people make New Year’s resolutions, they often leave it to fate to see whether those goals will be achieved. However, a person with a vision board can shape the board. Because they can create the board themselves, they are more than likely to take the steps necessary to achieve the goals because they’ve taken matters into their own hands.

Vision boards are a fun and creative way to embrace various aspects of life that people want to improve. They may also be an excellent way for people to make and track new goals for the future. Not only will a person feel like they’re moving forward in life, but they may also embrace the new year with hope and anticipation that the future may look brighter after all.
